result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 1 FOUND, 4 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Reviewed production authentication, BCrypt encoding, runtime datasource configuration, Docker/Compose, Oracle grants, environment example, and tracked documentation credential references. Actual production passwords are required environment inputs; placeholder/example and test-only values are not reported as production embedded secrets. No fixed encryption/signing key or effective hardcoded password was found; constant default usernames alone are not secret credentials. Oracle grants are schema-local CREATE privileges, not DBA or system-wide ANY permissions. Public gallery read access is explicitly intended in SecurityConfig and is not classified as unintended permission assignment. Credentials are redacted in all assessment evidence. External logging/deployment controls are unknown.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
values.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
values.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

values.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
values.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

values.name: Insufficient Logging

evidence.explanation: SecurityConfig.securityFilterChain:46-59 enables HTTP Basic for upload/delete but configures no authentication failure handler, authentication/authorization event listener, security audit repository, or request audit logger. No other production source defines such a listener. Default Spring Security successful/failed Basic-auth diagnostics are DEBUG, while supplied logging configuration enables DEBUG for application/Spring Web only (application.properties:32-34) and restricts Spring Web to WARN in Docker (application-docker.properties:29-32); Spring Security remains at default INFO. Failed credentials are rejected in the security filter before upload/delete controller logging, so brute-force/unauthorized attempts have no persistent security audit record under the supplied configuration. DetailController.deletePhoto:67-75 records only photo ID/result without requesting principal or client address. This concerns application-provided/default logging; an external ingress/SIEM could supply additional logging, but none is represented in this repository. No credential values are included.

values.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
values.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.
